ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a rectangular garden, divided by equal-sized square grids into 10 columns and 2 rows. The starting point S is at the lower-left corner. The arrows in the figure show one snail climbing upward from S along the left side, at a speed of 1 m/h; another snail climbing rightward from S along the bottom side, at a speed of 2 m/h. The upper side of the rectangle is marked A, B, C, D, among which D is at the upper-right corner, and B is located at the 6th unit on the upper side counted from the left side. Reasoning: According to the method given in the problem, regard the outer boundary of the rectangle as the snails' crawling route. The outer perimeter of the garden is 2 × (10 + 2) = 24 grid-side-length units. The speed ratio of the two snails is 1:2, and they start from S and crawl around the outer boundary in opposite directions, so when they first meet, the slow snail has traveled 1/3 of the full perimeter, and the fast snail has traveled 2/3 of the full perimeter. 1/3 of the full perimeter is 24 ÷ 3 = 8 units. The slow snail goes upward from S, first along the left side for 2 units to the upper-left corner, then along the upper side rightward for 6 units, reaching mark B. Therefore the position where the two snails first meet is B.

raw_record.question_text: A garden is split into equally sized square-shaped lots. One snail crawls 1 m per hour and the other crawls 2 m per hour. According to the labeled diagram, at which position will the two snails meet for the first time?

method.method_draft: Use the outer border as the snails' track and split the perimeter by the speed ratio. From the image, the garden rectangle is 10 equal square widths long and 2 square widths high; S is the lower-left corner. One snail leaves S upward along the left side, while the other leaves S to the right along the bottom and then continues around the outside. The perimeter is 2(10+2)=24 grid-side units. Since the speeds are 1 m/h and 2 m/h, by the time they first meet after leaving S, the slow snail has covered one third of the perimeter and the fast snail two thirds. One third of 24 is 8 units. Starting from S upward, 8 units means 2 units up the left side and then 6 units along the top edge. The top point 6 grid units from the left is labeled B.

method.method_draft: Compute and compare the arrival times to the labeled candidate points. From the image, along the slow snail's upward-then-top route from S, the distances to the top labels are: A = 2 up + 5 across = 7 units, B = 2 + 6 = 8 units, C = 2 + 7 = 9 units, and D = 2 + 10 = 12 units. Convert distance to time using the text speeds: slow time equals its distance/1, fast time equals its distance/2. Only at B do the times match: 8/1 = 16/2 = 8 hours, so the first meeting among the labeled positions is B.

Since its speed is 2 m/h, its arrival times are A = 8.5 h, B = 8 h, C = 7.5 h, D = 6 h.

The only labeled point where both snails arrive at the same time is B, where both take 8 hours. Therefore, they meet first at B.
